'''''Ceramium botryocarpum''''' is a small red marine [[alga]] in the Division Rhodophyta.<ref name ="Maggs">Maggs, C.A. and Hommersand, M.H. 1993. ''Seaweeds of the British Isles Volume 1 Rhodophyta Part 3A Ceramiales.'' {{ISBN|0-11-310045-0}}</ref>

==Description==
''Ceramium botryocarpum'' is a small filamentous branched alga growing as tufts to a height of 12 cm. The axial branches consist of large barrel shaped cells,<ref>Jones, W.E. 1962. A key to the genera of British Seaweeds. ''Field Studies'' Volume 1 No 4</ref> which branch irregularly dichotomously. The tips of the branches have strongly in inrolled apices. The axes are covered by small cells which form a complete cortex over the filaments. The axes appears banded due to the thinner covering of cortical cells at the internodes. Unlike certain other species of ''Ceramium'' it does not bear spines.<ref name ="Maggs"/>

==Habitat==
To be found in rock pools in the lower littoral.<ref>Bunker, F.StP.D, Maggs, C.A., Brodie, J.A., Bunker, A.R. 2017 ''Seaweeds of Britain and Ireland.'' Second Edition. Wild Nature Press, Plymouth. UK. {{ISBN|978-0-9955673-3-7}}</ref> Epiphytic on other small algae where there are larger brown are not present.<ref name="Maggs"/>

==Distribution==
Recorded from [[Ireland]] and [[Great Britain]], but probably under-recorded.<ref>Hardy, F.G. and Guiry, M.D. 2003. ''A Check-list and Atlas of the Seaweeds of Britain and Ireland.'' The British Phycological Society. {{ISBN|0-9527115-16}}</ref> Also recorded from the [[Channel Isles]] and [[France]].<ref name="Maggs"/>
